note: Phone beat as a conversation. The player talks instead of picking Safe/Unsafe. Ends map to v1 choice ids: phone-code, phone-hangup.

sms.text: Your Harbor sign-in code is 482 913. Never share this code. IT will never ask you for it.
sms.why: The text itself says IT will never ask for the code.

idle_line: Hello? You still there? This thing expires in like twenty seconds.

open.say: Hi, this is Dan from IT. We just blocked a sign-in on your account from overseas. I'm locking it down now. Read me the six-digit code that just hit your phone. Quick, before it expires.

name.say: Dan. Dan Reyes, service desk. Look, it's expiring.

ext.say: 4101. Can we do this? Your account is getting hammered right now.

why.say: To prove it's you before I kick the attacker out. Standard procedure, I do this ten times a night.

callback.say: There's no time for that. The code dies in thirty seconds. If they get in, they've got your email and your payroll.

push.say: Fine. When your paycheck bounces Friday, that's on you. Last chance, read me the code.

ask_why.label: Why do you need my code?

callback.label: Let me call you back on the service desk number.

refuse.label: I'm not reading a code over the phone.

hold.label: No. I'll call the service desk myself.

IT Service Desk.why: The real service desk is ext 4100. Nobody has 4101.

callback.say: Service desk. No, nobody here called you. We never ask for codes, ever. I'm locking your session and flagging it. Thanks for calling it in.

tells.why: The text with the code says IT will never ask for it.
Caller ID said ext 4101. The real service desk is 4100.
Thirty seconds, payroll, your fault: pressure so you don't stop and check.
You called the real number back. That's the move.
